name: Grade 9 IIIT: STEM Prototype Project
description: STEM project problems, users, constraints, proposals, tools, sketches, Tinkercad concepts, materials, test criteria, project logs, prototypes, proof of concept, improvements, limitations, evidence, and presentations.

words.definition: A need or challenge a project tries to solve.
words.example: The STEM project problem was connected to school safety.

words.definition: A person who will use or benefit from a design.
words.example: The users were students in the classroom.

words.definition: A limit or requirement that affects a design.
words.example: Class time was one constraint.

words.definition: A plan that explains a project problem, goal, tools, tests, and evidence.
words.example: The proposal listed the materials and test criteria.

words.definition: The result a project is trying to achieve.
words.example: The goal was to create a useful prototype.

words.definition: A material, platform, or app used to build a project.
words.example: Tinkercad was one approved tool.

words.definition: A 3D design tool used to build digital models.
words.example: The concept model was made in Tinkercad.

words.definition: A quick drawing that plans a design.
words.example: The proposal included a sketch.

words.definition: An early idea for how a solution could work.
words.example: The concept showed the main parts.

words.definition: The physical or digital resources needed for a project.
words.example: The materials list included cardboard and sensors.

words.definition: Standards used to decide if a prototype works.
words.example: The project used three test criteria.

words.definition: A test version of a product or solution.
words.example: The prototype was improved after testing.

words.definition: A small test that shows an idea can work.
words.example: The proof of concept showed the sensor could detect motion.

words.definition: A record of planning, building, testing, and reflection.
words.example: The logbook included photos and results.

words.definition: Helpful comments about strengths and changes.
words.example: Feedback helped refine the prototype.

words.definition: A change that makes a project better.
words.example: The improvement made the model stronger.

words.definition: A weakness or boundary that affects a project.
words.example: The prototype limitation was battery life.

words.definition: Information that supports a result or claim.
words.example: Photos and test results were evidence.

words.definition: A guide that explains how work will be evaluated.
words.example: The rubric included testing and reflection.

words.definition: A clear demonstration and explanation of work.
words.example: The presentation explained problem, design, tests, and improvement.
